findings.title: Exit-code split and the day-helper extraction are correct and verified
findings.description: `TickDatabaseUnreachable` subclasses `TickPreflightError`, so 223's writers keep exit 1 through `exit_code_for`, while `run_mapped` checks its `storage` tuple *before* `exit_code_for` (`tick_store_cmds.py:73-76`), giving `status`/`coverage` exit 4. I confirmed both branches against `tick_exit.py:50` and `store_context.py:164`, and the integration test `test_an_unreachable_tick_database_exits_4` covers both verbs. The `_utc_midnight` → `utc_midnight` promotion plus the new `days_touched` is behavior-preserving: `session_days` still applies the `start <= day < end` clip on the same set (`session_days.py:55-56`), and `ingest_plan.py:95` now calls the identical construction. The blanket `except Exception` in `run_mapped` is a documented process boundary (rule (c)), not a swallowed exception.

findings.title: The raw `tick_trade` scan is not shape-filtered, unlike every other read
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts *every* row in `tick_trade` inside the session windows with no join to `tick_request`/`tick_archive_unit`, while its four sibling reads all filter through `_SHAPE_WHERE` (`status_reads.py:55-60`) and the module docstring frames them as "which units and ledger rows are its own". `build_coverage` then compares that product-agnostic count against `ledger_totals(..., shape_of(entry), ...)`: `_session_row` (`tick_coverage.py:75-89`) builds its instrument set from the *union* of the two dicts, so any foreign row becomes a `(ledger 0, raw N)` pair, marks the session `mismatch`, names a foreign instrument, and exits 3. Supersession deletes replaced rows (`ingest_worker.py:120-135`), so this cannot fire today with the single-product `TICK_UNIVERSE` (`universe.py:38`), but slice 231 adds GC to `FUTURES_PRODUCT_CALENDAR` writing into the same table, and the module docstring's promise that `coverage` is "a raw-count proof for a date range" would then be false for ES. `tick_trade.unit_id` is present, so the fix is a join against the shape, as the other reads do.

findings.title: SQL constants in `status_reads.py` are un-annotated `str`, breaking the package's `LiteralString` idiom
findings.description: `_UNITS`, `_LEDGER_UNITS` and `_SHAPE_WHERE` are declared without the `LiteralString` annotation that every other SQL-bearing module in this package uses — `manifest_reads.py:36,84,90-91,167`, `manifest_repo.py:163,174`, `ingest_select.py:63`, `store_context.py:172` — including for constants that are themselves interpolated. psycopg3 types `execute`'s first parameter as `Query = LiteralString | SQL | Composed`, and an f-string built from a `str` constant is `str`, so the five `await conn.execute(f"...", ...)` calls here (lines 83, 100, 133, 165) are the calls most likely to fail the project's stated bar, "mypy clean on touched files" (`pyproject.toml:71-73`). I could not run mypy in this review, so treat the *compile-time* failure as unverified; what is verified is the definite inconsistency with the idiom used one module away for the same job. The same loosening appears at the CLI boundary, where `_read`/`read` take the connection as `Any` (`tick_store_cmds.py:155-170`) although the dedicated `Conn` alias exists and is the declared parameter type of `build_status`/`build_coverage`.

findings.title: Each product runs the unbounded `shape_units` and `contract_lines` queries once more than needed
findings.description: `_product_status` reaches `shape_units` twice per product — once directly through `_scope` (`tick_status_build.py:155`) and again inside `session_verdicts` at line 88 — and neither call is bounded by a date range ("Every current tier unit of the shape", `status_reads.py:80`). `contract_lines` is likewise unbounded. The manifest is small today, so this is not a cost problem now; it is a duplicated read that will grow with the archive, and the two call sites could share one fetch.

findings.title: `_JSON_OPTION`, `_DATE_FORMAT` and the `--start`/`--end` options are declared twice in the same Typer group
findings.description: `tick.py:74` and `tick_store_cmds.py:56` each define `_DATE_FORMAT = "%Y-%m-%d"`, and `--json` is declared as `_JSON_OPTION` in both modules for commands registered on the same `tick_app`. The two `--start/--end` pairs differ only in whether they are required and in their help text, so the shared literals can drift independently. The project rule on one value / one source is aimed at comparison values, so this is a note rather than a defect — but the option help and format are exactly the kind of thing that drifts silently between the writer verbs and the read verbs.

findings.title: The new render module has no direct tests; `age()`'s branches are unexercised
findings.description:
`tick_status_render.py` is covered only indirectly through `test/integration/data/test_tick_status_cli.py`, which asserts three substrings, the JSON shape, and the mismatch line. `age()` (`tick_status_render.py:45-51`) is the one piece of non-trivial logic in the module and none of its three branches is pinned: `test_tick_status_build.py` uses an edge age of exactly 3600 s (the minutes fall-through), so the `Nd Nh` and sub-hour paths — including the degenerate "0m" for a fresh edge — have no test. Rendering is low risk, so this is informational; a small parametrized test on `age()` would close it.

Sources outside the diff that back these findings: `src/manta_trading/data/tick/manifest_reads.py`, `manifest_repo.py`, `ingest_select.py`, `ingest_worker.py`, `tick_status.py`, `universe.py`, `ingest_plan.py`, `store_context.py`, `cli/commands/tick_exit.py`, `market/schema/migrations/tick.py`, `pyproject.toml`, and `project-documents/user/slices/225-slice.ingest-pass-and-proof-parity.md` (TD9–TD11, "Provides to Other Slices" — 231 GC).
